research_goal: Create level-based wrestling teaching, assessment, promotion, hold, and regression logic for SFTC across folkstyle, freestyle, Greco-Roman, and general wrestling development.

source_refs.title: USA Wrestling Core Curriculum
source_refs.notes: Used for skill progression and foundational wrestling literacy.

source_refs.title: United World Wrestling Regulations for Olympic Wrestling
source_refs.notes: Used for freestyle and Greco progression context.

technical_principles.summary: A wrestler can be intermediate in neutral attacks but beginner on bottom, top, par terre, or Greco upper-body work. Retrieval should unlock advanced drills by domain readiness.
Wrestling should progress from solo mechanics to cooperative partner drills, to controlled resistance, to short live goes, to full live wrestling.
A folkstyle athlete may still be beginner in Greco par terre or freestyle exposure defense. Style-specific readiness should be assessed separately.

beginner.definition: Learning safe stance, motion, level change, hand fighting, basic shots, sprawls, top pressure, bottom base, and wrestling rules.

intermediate.definition: Connecting attacks, defense, top/bottom, and match situations under controlled resistance.
locked: advanced opponent-specific systems without base skill
hard throw training without safe mechanics

advanced.definition: Individualized systems by style, opponent, weight class, score state, calendar, and readiness.
locked: hard live volume with poor readiness

common_errors: treating wrestling level as one global label
starting live wrestling before stance and defense are safe
teaching complex scrambles before base and sprawl competence
ignoring style differences between folkstyle, freestyle, and Greco
progressing volume when pain and readiness signals are poor
safety_constraints: No high-amplitude throw progressions until safe falling and partner control are reliable.
No high-volume shots with knee, hip, groin, or low-back pain.
No hard live wrestling with neck, neurological, severe head, or radiating symptoms.
Regression should preserve wrestling specificity when possible.

sport_training_rules.rule: Assess wrestling readiness by domain: neutral, hand fighting, takedown offense, takedown defense, top, bottom, par terre, scramble, S&C, and match IQ.
recommended_action: Use beginner drills in weak domains even when the athlete is advanced elsewhere.
Unlock live intensity only after technical and safety gates are met.
blocked_action: Do not unlock advanced throws, scrambles, or live volume from a global intermediate label alone.

planning_rules.rule: Select wrestling drills by domain readiness and style, not only by global experience.
recommended_action: Use beginner bottom work for a strong neutral wrestler with poor escapes.
Use Greco-specific upper-body domains when the user selects Greco.
blocked_action: Do not prescribe leg attacks for Greco-specific users.
Do not prescribe advanced scrambles for beginners.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build safe wrestling literacy across stance, motion, hand fighting, shots, sprawls, top, bottom, and basic rules.
Connect neutral attacks, defense, top/bottom, and match situations under controlled resistance.

skill_assessments.summary: Assess wrestling readiness by domain and style instead of one global label.
hold_if: unsafe falling or mat return behavior
knee, hip, groin, shoulder, rib, or back pain worsens

minimum_evidence: stance, motion, level change, penetration step, sprawl, and top/bottom basics are reliable
no worsening neck, shoulder, rib, back, hip, knee, ankle, or neurological symptoms
completion and RPE trends are inside target range
promote_when: can execute basic attacks and defenses under light resistance
can build base and escape safely
can follow style-specific rules and safety cues
hold_when: skill quality collapses under low fatigue
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock controlled resistance, chain wrestling, short live goes, and style-specific technical blocks.

minimum_evidence: 8+ additional weeks or 16+ completed wrestling/S&C sessions
can chain attacks, defend, reattack, ride/turn or escape under resistance
understands style-specific scoring and match tactics
live volume and recovery are managed
promote_when: can use opponent-specific tie or position systems
can adjust by score, time, edge, and style
can tolerate planned live and S&C load
hold_when: pain or readiness markers are poor
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock advanced style-specific systems, opponent planning, and competition block design.
